answer: An agent economy can price Sybils out with quadratic renewal fees tied to funding rails: every identity must periodically renew by paying from its funding source, and the fee for identities sharing one source grows with the square of the cluster size — a lone honest agent pays a velvet-soft base rate, while a farm of a thousand fakes on one island of wallets pays a million times more. Past the nadir where farming stops paying for itself, the attacker must either fund each fake through genuinely separate rails or abandon the farm.
